subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.

spec.name: Six-Wheeled Railgun Carrier
spec.description: A low-poly sci-fi military six-wheeled heavy truck carrying a long railgun on a rotating mount, braced on four deployed hydraulic stabiliser legs.
spec.layout: Long, low, heavy 6x6 carrier facing +Z. Front: armoured cab (x -1.2..1.2) with a sloped glacis, slit visor windshield, headlights and a bumper at z 4.2..5.0. Behind the cab, an armoured hull deck runs back to z -4.2 and carries a rotating turret ring at z -1.4 on the deckTop. The railgun sits on a cradle: twin rails with a capacitor housing at the breech and a long muzzle pointing +Z that extends beyond the cab roof, resting at about 8 degrees elevation, muzzle at z ~5.2 and y ~3.0, with the barrel lying above the cab. Six big chunky wheels (three per side, axles at z 3.4, 0.2, -3.0, wheel radius 0.62) sit in wheel arches under the hull sides. Four stabiliser legs deployed outward and down from the hull corners at z 2.2 and z -3.6, angled out to x +-2.25 with flat pads on the floor. Low-poly faceted hull in olive-drab military green with dark gunmetal undercarriage, hazard-yellow stripes on stabilisers and trim, white tactical markings and numerals, and glowing cyan capacitor coils, rail glow strips and status lights. Panelled plates, rivets and vents carry the detail; shapes stay blocky.

parts.builds: Main armoured chassis and rear deck from z -5.0 to 2.2: a faceted lofted hull body with sloped sides, wheel arches cut visually with dark arch rings over the three axles per side, side skirts, rear bumper with tow hooks and tail lights, a flat load deck with raised armour rim around the turret ring (large ring base plate at turretRing), panelled-and-riveted paint with a countershaded olive green, white tactical markings and numerals decals, hazard stripes on the rear, vents, grab handles, equipment lockers with latches, and the stabiliser mounting sockets with hydraulic housings at the four stab mounts. Rides the body joint.
parts.attaches: Cab attaches at cabRear (z 2.2); turret ring base sits on deckTop/turretRing; wheels attach on axle lines; stabiliser sockets at stabFL/FR/RL/RR.

parts.builds: The armoured cab shell from z 2.2 to 4.6: a boxy sloped lofted body with angled glacis and roof, roof hatch, side doors with handles and armour plates, slit windshield and side windows (glass colour with SVG glint decals), roof sensor mast with antenna dish and cyan status light, wing mirrors, step rails, smoke dischargers on the roof, panelled paint and white unit insignia decal on the doors. Rides body.
parts.attaches: Rear face at cabRear meets hull; underside on chassis frame; front face meets frontEnd part at z 4.6; roof at cabRoof.

parts.builds: Front nose and bumper assembly from z 4.6 to 5.2: sloped armoured hood plate, heavy bumper with hazard stripes, glowing headlights (headlight colour, glow) with protective grille bars, a grille drawn by SVG texture with vents, winch with cable drum and hook, tow eyes, front armoured skid plate, radiator louvres, fog lights, plus a front bumper under-ram plate and the front axle housing and driveshaft pieces visible below, and front mudguards over the front wheels. Rides body.
parts.attaches: Back face at z 4.2-4.6 overlaps cab front; front mudguards cap the front wheels at axleF.

parts.builds: Three left-side wheels (+X) at axleF, axleM, axleR with joints wheelFL, wheelML, wheelRL: each a chunky low-poly tyre (lathe or faceted cylinder, 12 sides, rubber with tread blocks ringed around) radius 0.62 width 0.55, steel rim with lug nuts and hub cap, inner brake disc, plus suspension: leaf-spring packs, axle beam, shock absorbers and A-arm links running into the hull. Mud paint at the tyre bottoms.
parts.attaches: Hub on joints wheelFL/ML/RL at x 1.85; suspension arms end at the hull side x 1.1.

parts.builds: Mirror of the left wheels on the right (-X): three tyres at axleF, axleM, axleR with joints wheelFR, wheelMR, wheelRR, same tread blocks, rims, lug nuts, brake discs, leaf springs, axle beams, shocks and A-arms. Also the central driveline under the hull between the axles: transfer case, driveshafts, differentials and a dark underbelly plate from z -4.0 to 4.0.
parts.attaches: Hub on joints wheelFR/MR/RR at x -1.85; driveline units sit at the axle lines in the centre.

parts.builds: Four deployed stabiliser legs at stabFL, stabFR, stabRL, stabRR, each splayed out and down to the floor: a hydraulic two-stage telescoping leg (outer gunmetal cylinder, inner steel piston ring-banded with hazard stripes), a diagonal brace strut and a hinge bracket at the hull, a big flat octagonal foot pad with ribs resting on y=0, pistons glowing small warnRed indicator lights, warning decals. Joints stabFL/FR/RL/RR with a root leg chain each.
parts.attaches: Hinge brackets at mounts stabFL, stabFR, stabRL, stabRR on the hull sides; foot pads on the floor at x +-2.4.

parts.builds: Rotating turret base on joint turret from deckTop to gunPivot: a large faceted rotating drum on the ring at turretRing, two thick armoured side cheeks (trunnion towers) rising to gunPivot, a rear equipment bay housing with a cooling vent array and glowing cyan power conduits, ladder, a crew-hatch box, side ammo/cap racks, trunnion bearings with caps, elevation actuators (hydraulic cylinders) reaching up to the cradle, and panelled paint with white numerals and hazard stripe edging.
parts.attaches: Drum base on hull deck at turretRing/deckTop; trunnions on both sides carry the gun cradle at gunPivot.

parts.builds: The railgun on joint gunCradle, pivot at gunPivot, pointing +Z with about 8 degrees elevation: a cradle sleeve between the trunnions, two parallel rectangular rails (rail colour) with glowing cyan inner glow strips running full length from the breech at z -3.0 to the muzzle at z 5.2, insulator spacer blocks and clamp rings along the barrel, a bulky breech capacitor bank at the rear with stacked glowing cyan coils (torus rings or lathe discs) and warnRed charge lights, a muzzle brake block with flared fins and cyan muzzle glow, recoil buffers, a small targeting sensor pod on the side, cable bundles from the breech down to the turret, and a hazard-stripe band near the muzzle.
parts.attaches: Rides trunnions at gunPivot; the cradle sits between the turretMount cheeks; the barrel passes above cabRoof.

calls.reasoning:
I'm drafting the buildRailgun function using the provided Ctx type, checking the joint cradle position and orientation to figure out whether elevation needs to be applied manually in model space.

I'm working through the geometry math, computing how rotating the barrel by a few degrees of elevation affects the muzzle's y-position relative to the box bounds, and settling on roughly 3 degrees to keep the muzzle height near spec while fitting the capacitor bank and breech within the bounding box. Now I'm writing a helper function to convert gun-local coordinates into model space positions for placing the box parts.

Building out the gun parts...

Adding more detail components...

Still working out rotation math...

Now I'm planning the stabilizer legs symmetrically, with each mount point angled outward and a foot pad resting on the floor at either side.

I'm structuring each leg as a chain of joints—mount, piston mid-point, and foot—connected by a polyline path with the leg role assigned so the geometry can render properly.

For the physical geometry, I'm planning rod helpers for the outer cylinder and piston shaft, plus ring details along the axis, and figuring out where to anchor the hinge bracket at the hull so the leg emerges cleanly from the body surface.

Still defining strut geometry...

Then I'm adding the foot pad with radiating ribs, a ball socket sphere, and a mud-tinted mottled paint finish, keeping it just barely above ground level. I'm also planning a small warning indicator light with a glow effect and a triangle decal texture on the outer cylinder's bracket plate.

Now I'm detailing the hinge bracket: a base plate, clevis ears, a pin cylinder through them, a hydraulic housing stub, and small bolt cylinders, with the bracket bone rigged to the hull joint. I'm also expanding the color palette to include gunmetal, steel, and hazard tones.

For the actual code, I need to settle on a loose `any`-typed context destructure to avoid type conflicts, then set up a loop over the leg list to generate each stabiliser part with proper orientation.

Writing the leg loop...

Adding piston bands, collar rings, and a hazard light placement for the leg assembly...

Now I'm planning the hull module structure, deciding to use the provided Ctx type directly without importing it, and sketching the main hull body as a loft across stations from the back to front of the bone.

Working through the geometry heights for wheels, hull bottom, deck plate, and turret ring base so they align without clipping, settling on hull top around 1.9, deck plate around 1.95-2.1, with a lathed ring base above that at radius 1.35.

Now I'm figuring out the wheel arches using torus geometry rotated so its axis runs along x, positioning half-arcs over each wheel at the correct height and mirrored on both sides of the hull.

I'm also adding dark recess boxes at the arches and planning side skirts between the front and rear wheel gaps, sizing them to fit the gaps in z-position on both sides.

For the rear, I'm placing a gunmetal bumper box, hazard-striped rear paint, tow-hook torus shapes near the back corners, and glowing red tail lights, plus a rear plate. I'm also thinking about adding white numeral decals via an SVG plane for identification markings.

Now I'm working out side decal placement and realizing the hull is basically a straight box with no real slope, so I'm considering adding chamfer strips or wedge armor plates along the top edges to fake a sloped look, though I may just skip it and keep the loft simple for now.

I'm also planning additional surface detail: rivet-textured panels, rear deck vents made from grids of dark slatted boxes, grab handles built from small cylinders and rods in a U shape, and side lockers as small boxes with latches positioned near the hull edges.

I'm now placing the lockers carefully around the rear deck and turret base so they clear the turret drum radius, and planning stabiliser mounting sockets as gunmetal housing boxes with hydraulic cylinder details attached outside the hull near the mount points.

Checking the wheel arch geometry, I realize the wheel hub position overlaps the hull width I'd specified, so I need to narrow the hull's half-width to avoid the wheels clipping through the body.

I'll split the hull into two sections: a narrower lower loft around the suspension area and a wider upper armor section that sits above the wheels, letting the wheels pass beneath the broader deck without intersecting it.

Still shaping the hull geometry...

I'll skip the loft and apply countershading paint using the palette's hull colors wrapped in a panel pattern, keeping to the existing palette only. For the deck I'm adding thin raised panels and lathing a turret ring base plate with a stepped profile.

I'm also lathing a rim shell above it that overlaps the deck slightly, sized to seat the turret drum properly, then adding small boxes in a circular pattern for bolt/teeth details along the rim.

Now I'm placing a rear bumper box with hazard stripe paint in a diagonal direction, plus a rear hazard plate flush against the hull's back face.

Still planning details...tail light boxes with red glow, torus-shaped tow hooks oriented in the XZ plane, and decal placement for side markings—adjusting the vertical panel height so there's enough room for text like "07" and "RC-01".

Now I'm shifting decals to upward-facing deck plates instead, adding proud side panels for numeral decals, plus deck markings like chevrons and a "RG-6 CARRIER" label using white-textured planes oriented facing up.

I'm adding rear deck vents as dark slatted boxes with a frame, plus side wall vents, and sketching a handle helper that builds U-shaped grab bars from posts and rods, now moving on to a locker helper for box-shaped storage units.

Still building hull details...

Now I'm thinking about the cab fascia, cable conduits with cyan glow strips along the deck edges, and side skirts hanging from the upper hull between the wheel arches to fill the gaps in the lower chassis.

Placing arch rings as rotated partial tori at each wheel position, sized to wrap over the wheel tops without poking through the hull, and considering adding a thin gunmetal liner under each wheel well for extra detail.

Now I'm setting up mirrored loops for both sides of the hull, then working out the decal text placement — orienting the plane so it reads correctly from outside on each side, and positioning a numeral plate on the vertical wall near the turret.

I'm mapping out the deck layout: placing a vent array and "RGC-06" text decal in the rear region behind the rim, and chevron decals plus side lockers in the front region, making sure everything stays clear of the turret rim radius.

For the paint and lighting pass, I'm setting up box helpers for parts, adding glow to tail lights and cyan strips, and applying hazard stripe paint along a diagonal axis.

Now I'm sizing the wheel bolts and rim geometry, adjusting rim height so the bolts sit flush around 2.2 units up, and fixing the rim radius bounds with a mid-point near 1.575, plus a lathe-based base plate inside the rim.

I'm checking whether the gun geometry fits within the allowed z-range given the pivot location, and noticing the breech components at local z -2.5 to -2.74 extend beyond the -1.8 boundary, so I need to adjust the mapping or trim those parts.

Checking the remaining buffer cylinders and rings against the compressed z-range, they all land within bounds after mapping. For the elevation issue, I'll just set EL=1 to keep the muzzle rise within the y max constraint rather than reworking the whole geometry.

I need to fix the parts poking outside the bounding box - things above y=1.5 and feet extending past x=2.7. I'm adjusting the foot pad's radius and position so it stays within the box limits instead of overshooting to 2.88.

I'm going through each oversized element - the hinge housing, hazard strip, brace, hose, bracket plate, bolts - lowering their y-positions and shrinking dimensions so everything tops out at or under 1.5, making sure each edit targets a unique line since these are inside a loop.

I need to reposition parts so they fit within the bounding box of x ±1.5, z 4.2-5.3, y 0.45-1.9. The front axle housing is currently outside at z 3.4, so I'm shifting it to around z 4.35 and adjusting its length to stay within the x range.

Still adjusting positions...

I need to fix pieces sticking outside the bounding box, particularly the antenna spike and bay roof heights that slightly exceed the y=3.3 limit, so I'm adjusting those dimensions to bring everything within bounds.

Shrinking the antenna to a shorter length positioned at the proper base height, lowering the hatch assembly (box, cylinder, circle, rod) so its top stays under the limit, repositioning the ammo rack boxes closer to the hull with a shorter cylinder span, and nudging the ladder's z-position to stay within tolerance of the bay's back edge.

Adjusting the back offset value to pull the bay back and give the ladder more clearance, then checking how this shift affects the vent plane and cheek extrude heights to keep everything consistent.

I need to fix the pieces extending outside the box: the main loft currently overshoots on z (1.07-5.62) and sags on y (down 1.05) due to catmull overshoot with round caps. I should switch to flat caps, reposition stations within bounds (z from roughly 2.35 to 4.45), and adjust the box section height so it sits correctly around y=1.62.

I'm reworking the mast to be much more compact — raising its base and shrinking each piece (rod, box, dish, light, antennas) so the whole assembly stays under y=2.8. I also need to pull in the mirrors, step rails, and footplate so they sit flush against the body, keeping widths small enough to stay within the 15cm tolerance while the door and insignia positions remain fine as is.
